paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the King counts what is done for His people as done for Him. He says, "whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me." (Matthew 25:40) Hungry, thirsty, a stranger, naked, sick, in prison: He names real needs, and He says what was done for one of the least of these was done for Him.

Now look at what surprised BOTH groups. The righteous ask, "Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You…?" (Matthew 25:37) and the ones on the left ask, "Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?" (Matthew 25:44) Both groups ask "when," so both are surprised to hear it was about Him. A meal, a drink, a visit: the King says those moments were never little to Him.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery: what we do for the least of these is never small to the King, and neither is what we leave undone. He says, "whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for Me." (Matthew 25:45) Jesus lands this teaching with two places to go: "eternal punishment" or "eternal life." (Matthew 25:46) This is why my ovens stay ready, friend, and a ready baker keeps their eyes open for the least of these. The teaching on the Mount of Olives wraps up here, so Jesus has now said all of it.
